findings.title: SPEC.md §5.1 rule 2 does not record the sanctioned surrogate-safe truncation semantics
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC.md §5.1 sanitization rule 2: 'Truncate string values to 255 characters.' (echoed at §7.1 and §11 note 4)
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js sanitizeTrackingValue (3 lines added by fix commit fa51c91a5): after .slice(0, 255), a trailing lone high surrogate (charCode 0xD800-0xDBFF) is dropped, yielding 254 code units at that boundary. The code is the sanctioned qa-run-2 Layer-2 l2-B1 HIGH fix (lone-surrogate JSON escape caused the entire signup POST to 400) — delta-reviewed and approved in the prior run (reviews/QA-COMPLETE.md) — but SPEC.md was amended only for D18/D19, never for this. Layer 1 criterion: the change does not trace to the spec text; a re-implementer following §5.1 literally would reintroduce the 400.
corroborated_by: agent-15 (noted as QA-sanctioned but exceeding the spec's literal text)
findings.recommendation: Amend SPEC.md — not the code. Update §5.1 rule 2 to record the approved semantics (truncate to 255 code units, then drop a trailing lone high surrogate left by the slice), with provenance (fix commit fa51c91a5, qa-run-2 l2-B1). Per the stale-references-after-amendments failure pattern, update every other reference to the truncation rule in the same amendment (§7.1, §11 note 4) so no stale '255' text remains that contradicts the recorded semantics.

spec_coverage.notes: Every SPEC.md numbered requirement (§2-§11) was traced by at least two agents; agent-14 built the full 22-file reverse mapping table and agent-15 the full forward coverage table. Only untraceable diff content across the entire range: the 3 surrogate-truncation lines above. The decode-uri-component key-scan (fix 299cf9465) was examined by agents 7, 8, 14, 15 and judged traceable: §5.1 declares the key-scan mechanism plan-level ('the contract is: order comes from the raw string, values from the parse'), and the decoder-agreement is part of that mechanism.
